Kindscope

A small language model reading a story, drawn so you can walk around it. The model reads one letter at a time and passes it up through 13 stages; each stage adds something. Drag to turn it. Click a block to see which earlier characters the looking-back stages draw on there. Switch what the height shows: how much each stage adds, or how much breaks if you take that stage out. They are not the same, and that is the first thing this model teaches. Pick a finding below to see where in the model it lives.

One prompt, passing through GoldWorm

Stand at one byte of a story and look down the model. Each block adds something to a running state; the lengths below are what each added here. The shading under the text is how hard the next byte was to predict.

Story

How much each block wrote at this byte, in the order the model adds them (depth runs down). Length is how much a block wrote here, not how much it matters: the last block writes most, and removing the first rewriting block does eight times the damage.

Reading the same site four ways

These readings mean something only at one kind of place: the byte just before a word that follows “the” or “a” (outlined in the text above). There, after each rewriting stage, how far the state sits from a typical such place, in standard deviations. Above zero leans toward an adjective coming next.
